resolutions: Cardinal numeral structure is vigesimal, with typed orders one, twenty, four hundred, and eight thousand.
A numeral Source may produce an ordinary NNC or enter a compatible NNC or VNC operation without an example-stem gate.
Ordinary and gross count remain distinct typed meanings rather than spelling variants.
Gross count uses the ix matrix and requires plural reference even with a nonanimate referent.
Ordinary count follows the normal animate or nonanimate subject-number restriction.
A compatible counting set is automatic when only one survives and is a user choice only when several survive.
Canvas examples prove counting-set grammar but never authorize a noun, verb, or productive route.
The fuller typed Source of one is the nounstem cem.
Free singular cē follows final-m loss with compensatory vowel length automatically.
Embedded one retains cem and applies its following-boundary assimilation automatically.
Animate plural one uses cem with m-eh rather than asking for a plural allomorph.
The cem Source enters compatible NNC and VNC compounds productively, independent of listed examples.
Contextual complete, entire, together, and forever readings do not become stem-admission rules.
Two, three, and four retain typed pronominal Sources ōme, ēyi, and nāhui.
Their ordinary animate plurals preserve the internal n and canonical t-in number dyad.
Their gross forms are ōme-x, ē-ix, and nāhu-ix with plural t-in.
Two embeds automatically as ōm where conditioned, while full ōme remains an exposed choice only where Canvas licenses it.
Three preserves free ēyi or yēyi and embedded ē, yē, or ēx as genuine positional alternatives rather than a stem list.
Four embeds as nāhu before a vowel and nāuh before a consonant automatically.
Vowel quantity, truncation, y or x realization, assimilation, and number dyads are derived from typed Source and boundary facts.
An unlicensed positional variant is blocked without changing the Source stem identity.
A mismatched counting set, gross singular, ordinary nonanimate plural, or gross one is blocked by typed grammar.
Caller formulas and surfaces cannot replace the canonical numeral owner.
Every accepted atom has an exact owner-issued writing or reading observation, mutation check, and clickable cue where applicable.
Five preserves the typed polymorphemic Source mā-cu-ī-l and its historical passive-patientive analysis.
Six through nine preserve the internal chicua, chiuc, or chic plus one-through-four composition rather than flattened example spellings.
Free, embedded, ordinary plural, and gross ix forms of five through nine are derived from typed value, position, and boundary facts.
The internal chicua-family allomorph, assimilation, ix, and number dyad are automatic rather than user choices.
Ten and fifteen preserve the typed Sources mah-tlāc and cax-tōl.
Their ordinary and gross forms are generated by the shared cardinal owner without an example-value list.
Only gross count may enter the Lesson 34 exceptional possessive-state construction.
An animate gross-count possessor must be grammatically plural.
A nonanimate gross-count possessor has third-person common-number grammar together with a typed plural referent.
The ti versus tin ending is exposed only for the documented nonanimate gross-count possessive ambiguity.
An animate possessor cannot select ti, and the application does not repair incompatible participant facts.
Higher vigesimal orders accept typed multipliers one through nineteen productively.
The fixed matrices pōhu-a-l, tzon, and xiqu-ipil preserve their morphemic Sources and meanings.
Multiplier shape, matrix selection, internal boundary, multiplication, and total value are derived automatically.
Secondary lexical readings such as many, mockingbird, or a possible cacao bagful remain reading evidence rather than numeral-route authority.
Changing valid Source shape while preserving the grammatical higher-order facts does not remove route eligibility.
Changing possessor identity, animacy, plurality, or acyclicity facts while holding the numeral Source constant blocks only the incompatible construction.
Canvas numeral witnesses prove productive structures and never authorize a closed inventory of values, nounstems, or verbstems.
Numeral conjunction orders canonical component Results from higher to lower.
Every rightward numeral conjunct receives short om as an additional-number relation, distinct from long ōm two.
Separate clauses and the licensed eleven-through-fourteen conjunctive compound are the only exposed conjunction-form choice.
Recursive conjunction preserves every owner-issued component Result and its typed Source.
Downgrading a numeral conjunction before a higher-order matrix deletes only its rightmost number position.
Numerals already bearing the same order matrix are not re-conjoined as though they were different ranks.
Rock, row, thing, and maize-cob classifiers operate on compatible typed Sources rather than listed nouns.
Classifier boundary changes such as nāuh plus pān and final l plus tla-man are automatic.
A rightward numeral conjunct does not repeat the classifier matrix.
The maize-cob set counts directly through nineteen and uses an owner-issued tlamic preterit-agentive Result from twenty through thirty-nine.
A copied or caller-written tlamic lookalike cannot satisfy the cob continuation requirement.
Classifier selection is constrained by typed referent compatibility only when such compatibility facts are supplied.
tecpān, ipil, and quimil productively count lined-up groups, piles, and bundles of twenty.
Their multiplier is derived from one through nineteen and their total value is computed automatically.
A lower remainder is composed by the same canonical higher-to-lower numeral conjunction.
People, animals, houses, rocks, blankets, paper, tortillas, and hides remain examples rather than route gates.
Changing an example referent label while keeping compatible grouping facts does not change authorization.
Groups 7 through 9 add no manual om, classifier-boundary, multiplication, deletion, or example-membership controls.
Affinity and distributive-varietal reduplication remain distinct through vowel length versus glottal evidence.
Reduplication meaning is a user choice only when the grammatical context leaves it unresolved.
Numeral reduplication scope follows morphemic structure and is never a manual scope control.
Seven through nine reduplicate both the embedded numeral and the basic numeral matrix.
Ten reduplicates the mahtlāc matrix, while numeral conjunction reduplicates every conjunct.
Classifier and number structure continue through the shared owners after reduplication.
Canah, quēn, and ahzo quēn modify a complete numeral clause with approximation meanings.
Oc modifies a complete numeral clause with another or more meaning.
The complete oc cē clause may enter the canonical supplementation owner as a supplementary subject.
English translations containing else do not create productive grammar routes.
Measure matrices remain open typed Sources rather than an example whitelist.
Amount versus length is retained as typed measure meaning and exposed only when genuinely unresolved.
A numeral measure compound is derived from the typed numeral and measure Source boundaries.
Measured composition requires owner-issued measure and measured-thing NNC Results.
The measure NNC is automatically principal in the licensed adjectival-modification relation.
Copied Results, caller formulas, and caller surfaces cannot authorize measured composition.
Changing an example measure stem while preserving valid typed measure facts preserves route eligibility.
Groups 10 through 12 add no manual reduplication-scope, boundary, principal-selection, example-measure, else-route, or formula controls.
